item.title: Agent Workflow Memory (AWM): How It Works and Results
item.description:
Agent workflow memory means an LLM agent keeps reusable routines learned from its own past runs and follows them on new tasks. The best-known version is Agent Workflow Memory (AWM) by Wang, Mao, Fried and Neubig (CMU and MIT, ICML 2025). AWM induces workflows from past trajectories and puts the relevant ones in the agent’s prompt.

On web navigation with GPT-4, the paper reports a 51.1% relative gain on WebArena and 24.6% on Mind2Web. This page explains how AWM builds workflows, the difference between its online and offline modes, the full results, the limits found by the authors and by later work, and how to build workflow memory into an agent today. Sources: the arXiv paper, the ICML 2025 proceedings version, and the official repo, checked on 12 October 2026.

item.title: Microsoft Memora: Agent Memory With Cue Anchors
item.description:
Microsoft Memora is a research memory system for AI agents from Microsoft Research. Its idea is to separate what is stored from how it is found: each memory keeps its full detail, but search runs only over a short summary (the primary abstraction) and a few tags (cue anchors). The paper was accepted at ICML 2026 and the code is MIT-licensed on GitHub.

This page explains how Memora works, what Microsoft reports about its results, how to try it, and where it sits next to production memory tools. Sources are the arXiv paper, the Microsoft Research blog post (June 29, 2026) and the microsoft/Memora repository.

item.title: LLM Memory Survey Papers: The 6 Worth Reading (2026)
item.description:
An LLM memory survey is a review paper that sorts the research on how language models and agents store, update and recall information. Six surveys on arXiv cover most of the field as of October 2026. Start with Zhang et al. (2024) for the basics, then read Hu et al.’s “Memory in the Age of AI Agents” (December 2025) for the current map.

Each one splits memory differently. That’s the useful part: the taxonomies show which questions the field treats as open. This page summarizes each survey from its arXiv paper, with links to the abstract and the full text.
